name: Harper Lee
bio: Harper Lee (1926–2016) was an American novelist whose debut, To Kill a Mockingbird, won the Pulitzer Prize and became one of the most widely read novels of the twentieth century.

name: Jane Austen
bio: Jane Austen (1775–1817) was an English novelist whose sharp social comedies of manners, including Pride and Prejudice, remain touchstones of English fiction.

name: George Orwell
bio: George Orwell (1903–1950) was an English essayist and novelist whose warnings against totalitarianism, above all Nineteen Eighty-Four, shaped modern political language.

name: F. Scott Fitzgerald
bio: F. Scott Fitzgerald (1896–1940) was an American writer of the Jazz Age whose masterpiece, The Great Gatsby, dissected wealth and the American dream.

name: Gabriel García Márquez
bio: Gabriel García Márquez (1927–2014) was a Colombian novelist and Nobel laureate, the leading voice of magical realism and author of One Hundred Years of Solitude.

name: Khaled Hosseini
bio: Khaled Hosseini (b. 1965) is an Afghan-American novelist and physician whose The Kite Runner brought Afghan history to millions of readers.

name: Haruki Murakami
bio: Haruki Murakami (b. 1949) is a Japanese novelist whose dreamlike, music-steeped fiction — including Norwegian Wood — has a devoted global readership.

name: Kazuo Ishiguro
bio: Kazuo Ishiguro (b. 1954) is a British–Japanese novelist and Nobel laureate known for The Remains of the Day and his studies of memory and restraint.

name: Agatha Christie
bio: Agatha Christie (1890–1976) was an English writer, the best-selling novelist in history, whose puzzles — from And Then There Were None onward — defined the genre.

name: Tana French
bio: Tana French (b. 1973) is an Irish novelist whose atmospheric Dublin Murder Squad books, beginning with In the Woods, reimagined the literary crime novel.

name: Stieg Larsson
bio: Stieg Larsson (1954–2004) was a Swedish journalist whose Millennium trilogy, led by The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo, became a worldwide phenomenon.

name: Raymond Chandler
bio: Raymond Chandler (1888–1959) was an American writer who gave the private-eye novel its poetry; The Big Sleep introduced Philip Marlowe.

name: Yuval Noah Harari
bio: Yuval Noah Harari (b. 1976) is an Israeli historian whose sweeping synthesis Sapiens became one of the most discussed history books of its decade.

name: Mary Beard
bio: Mary Beard (b. 1955) is a British classicist whose SPQR retells a thousand years of Roman history with wit and rigor.

name: Jared Diamond
bio: Jared Diamond (b. 1937) is an American geographer and biologist whose Guns, Germs, and Steel reframed the deep history of human societies.

name: Stephen Hawking
bio: Stephen Hawking (1942–2018) was an English theoretical physicist whose A Brief History of Time made cosmology a bestseller for a generation.

name: Carl Sagan
bio: Carl Sagan (1934–1996) was an American astronomer and science communicator whose Cosmos carried the wonder of science to millions.

name: Richard Dawkins
bio: Richard Dawkins (b. 1941) is a British evolutionary biologist whose The Selfish Gene changed how we think about natural selection.

name: Rebecca Skloot
bio: Rebecca Skloot (b. 1972) is an American science writer whose The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks fused reporting with a family story.

name: Rachel Carson
bio: Rachel Carson (1907–1964) was an American marine biologist whose Silent Spring launched the modern environmental movement.

name: Rupi Kaur
bio: Rupi Kaur (b. 1992) is a Canadian poet and illustrator whose collections milk and honey and The Sun and Her Flowers defined a new popular poetics.

name: Sylvia Plath
bio: Sylvia Plath (1932–1963) was an American poet whose collection Ariel remains one of the most electrifying volumes in modern poetry.

name: Daniel Kahneman
bio: Daniel Kahneman (1934–2024) was an Israeli–American psychologist and Nobel laureate whose Thinking, Fast and Slow mapped the two systems of the mind.

name: Susan Cain
bio: Susan Cain (b. 1968) is an American writer whose Quiet revalued introversion and changed how workplaces and schools think.

name: Jon Krakauer
bio: Jon Krakauer (b. 1954) is an American writer and mountaineer whose Into the Wild and Into Thin Air are classics of narrative nonfiction.

name: Alfred Lansing
bio: Alfred Lansing (1921–1975) was an American journalist whose Endurance tells Shackleton's Antarctic survival voyage with novelistic power.

name: E. H. Gombrich
bio: E. H. Gombrich (1909–2001) was an Austrian–British art historian whose The Story of Art has introduced millions to the history of images.

name: John Berger
bio: John Berger (1926–2017) was an English critic and novelist whose Ways of Seeing changed how we look at art and at looking itself.

name: Peter Thiel
bio: Peter Thiel (b. 1967) is an entrepreneur and investor whose Zero to One distills a contrarian philosophy of startups.

name: Jim Collins
bio: Jim Collins (b. 1958) is an American researcher of company performance whose Good to Great became a standard text of management.

name: Marcus Aurelius
bio: Marcus Aurelius (121–180) was Roman emperor and Stoic philosopher; his private notebook, Meditations, endures as a manual of self-command.

name: Viktor E. Frankl
bio: Viktor E. Frankl (1905–1997) was an Austrian psychiatrist and Holocaust survivor whose Man's Search for Meaning found purpose in the darkest places.

name: Jostein Gaarder
bio: Jostein Gaarder (b. 1952) is a Norwegian writer whose Sophie's World became the world's unlikely best-selling history of philosophy.

name: Albert Camus
bio: Albert Camus (1913–1960) was a French–Algerian writer and Nobel laureate whose The Myth of Sisyphus confronts absurdity with lucidity.

name: Suzanne Collins
bio: Suzanne Collins (b. 1962) is an American author whose Hunger Games trilogy reshaped young adult fiction for a generation.

name: Clayton M. Christensen
bio: Clayton M. Christensen (1952–2020) was an American scholar whose The Innovator's Dilemma gave business the theory of disruption.

name: Tracy Kidder
bio: Tracy Kidder (b. 1945) is an American narrative nonfiction writer whose The Soul of a New Machine captured engineering as human drama.

name: Walter Isaacson
bio: Walter Isaacson (b. 1951) is an American biographer whose acclaimed lives of Leonardo, Franklin, and Steve Jobs set the standard for the form.

name: Nelson Mandela
bio: Nelson Mandela (1918–2013) was a South African statesman whose Long Walk to Freedom is among the great autobiographies of the century.

name: Anne Frank
bio: Anne Frank (1929–1945) was a German–Dutch teenager whose diary, written in hiding in Amsterdam, became one of the world's most read books.

name: James Clear
bio: James Clear (b. 1986) is an American writer whose Atomic Habits became the definitive popular guide to behavior change.

name: Cal Newport
bio: Cal Newport (b. 1982) is an American computer scientist whose Deep Work argues that focus is the scarce skill of the modern economy.

name: Carol S. Dweck
bio: Carol S. Dweck (b. 1946) is an American psychologist whose Mindset introduced the growth mindset to education and business.
